title: Default Arguments
learningObjectives: Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: A default argument supplies a value for a trailing parameter when the caller omits it. Default values are normally written in the declaration visible to callers, not repeated in the definition.
understand.whyItMatters: Defaults simplify common calls while still allowing callers to customize less common behavior.
understand.explain: Required parameters must come before parameters with defaults. Keep defaults safe and unsurprising. Be careful when combining defaults with overloaded functions because some calls can become ambiguous.

examples.title: Default multiplier
examples.code: int scale(int value,int factor=2){return value*factor;}\n// scale(5) -> 10; scale(5,3) -> 15
examples.explanation: Omitting factor uses its default of two.

examples.title: Optional greeting prefix
examples.code: void greet(const std::string& name,const std::string& prefix=\"Hello\"){std::cout<<prefix<<\" \"<<name;}
examples.explanation: The caller can use the common prefix or provide another.

examples.title: Trailing default parameter
examples.code: int sum3(int a,int b,int c=0){return a+b+c;}\n// sum3(2,3) -> 5
examples.explanation: Only the trailing parameter is omitted.

examples.title: Explicit default override
examples.code: int multiply(int n,int times=3){int result=0;for(int i=0;i<times;++i)result+=n;return result;}\n// multiply(4,2) -> 8
examples.explanation: The call overrides the default repetition count.

examples.title: Default belongs in declaration
examples.code: int repeat(int value,int count=1);\n// definition: int repeat(int value,int count){...}
examples.explanation: Do not specify the same default again in the function definition.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Default Arguments examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Design a formatting helper with one required value and two trailing defaulted options. Test calls that omit both defaults, omit one, and explicitly override both.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.

questions.explanation: The omitted trailing parameter receives its default.
The visible declaration specifies the default.
Only trailing parameters can be omitted.
